palouse_ars.title: USDA ARS: Soil health and ecological resilience of no-till, organic, and mixed-crop livestock systems in eastern Washington State
palouse_ars.supports: Three-year spring pea → winter wheat → spring wheat sequence in the Palouse.
palouse_ars.limitations: Does not establish local planting/harvest dates or complete monthly cover.

winter_pea.title: WSU STEEP: Austrian Winter Pea a Good Alternative to Fallow
winter_pea.supports: Moscow trials included seed or green-manure Austrian winter pea → winter wheat → spring barley.
winter_pea.limitations: 1981–1985 trials; contemporary local suitability and management need review.

pea_traits.title: USDA NRCS Pullman Plant Guide: Pea
pea_traits.supports: Peas are legumes; symbiotic root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen. Austrian winter peas are adapted to cold temperatures.
pea_traits.limitations: Does not establish numeric frost tolerance, local water-need categories, or minimum season days.

silage.title: WSU Extension FS358E: Increasing Value of Corn Silage in Corn-Triticale System by Intercropping with Forage Soybean
silage.locator: Pages 1–2: Background and Prosser trial; page 4: planting guidance
silage.supports: Annual corn–triticale double cropping and forage-soybean intercropping; research near Prosser.
silage.limitations: Regional evidence, not a confirmed rotation on the demonstration field; no complete monthly cover calendar.

ecology.title: Washington Department of Ecology: Voluntary Clean Water Guidance, Crop Systems
ecology.supports: Lists corn–triticale–wheat as a rotation example subject to regional and site-specific factors.
ecology.limitations: Does not assign one crop per calendar year, identify wheat growth habit, or give a Yakima field schedule.

skagit.title: Washington Soil Health Initiative: Northwestern Washington Annual Cropping Systems
skagit.locator: Current Situation and soil physical properties
skagit.supports: Skagit-area potato-driven systems include small grains, silage corn and forages; growers consider cover crops and longer intervals.
skagit.limitations: No exact three-year sequences; do not infer crop order from the crop list.

nwrec.title: Washington Soil Health Initiative: Six sites, six unique soils, and sixteen crops
nwrec.locator: Northwest Washington Potato-Based Annual Cropping Systems LTARE site
nwrec.supports: Lists potato, spring barley, silage corn and winter wheat at Mount Vernon.
nwrec.limitations: A crop list is not a rotation sequence.

residue.title: WSU STEEP: New Minimum Tillage Systems for Legume-Winter Wheat Cropping Sequence
residue.locator: The Problem; Need for a 3-Year Rotation
residue.supports: Highlights limited legume residue and erosion risks; crop presence alone does not establish protective ground cover.
residue.limitations: Historical guidance; no field-specific cover fractions or erosion prediction.

fao_water.title: FAO Irrigation Water Management: Crop Water Needs
fao_water.supports: General seasonal water requirements and indicative growing periods.
fao_water.limitations: Not Washington-specific; not irrigation quantities or cultivar-specific maturity.

fao_roots.title: FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56
fao_roots.limitations: Unrestricted-soil potential; not measured roots at the demonstration points.

nonlegume_distinction.title: Government of Saskatchewan: Soil Improvements With Legumes
nonlegume_distinction.supports: Distinguishes nodulated nitrogen-fixing legumes from cereals and other non-legumes.
nonlegume_distinction.limitations: Botanical distinction only; regional management rates are not transferred to Washington.
